minutes.headline: Select Board appointed a conservation member, approved two Sept. 17 events, and dropped term limits; water talk postponed.
minutes.summary: The board approved a beer and wine license and a toll fundraiser, appointed a Conservation Commission member and ratified two town manager hires. The water district presentation on reactivating the Hickory Hills well was cut off by Zoom intrusions and moved to next Tuesday. The board discussed the appointment policy and leaned against term limits. Committee reports covered school busing and sidewalks, the municipal building committee's storage position, and the library trust funds.

budget_items.topic: Winter Recovery Assistance Program state funding
budget_items.what_was_said: Town received one-time state funding that must be spent by June 30, 2023 on road, sidewalk and signage work. Police detail costs are ineligible.
DPW director's rough plan splits the funds among striping, sidewalks, guardrails and a traffic signal controller.
A member relayed that buses this year cost a stated amount each, and the committee was weighing the cost of more busing next year.

budget_items.topic: Remodel cost estimates for town buildings
budget_items.what_was_said: Municipal building committee finding that remodel estimates run a stated range per square foot, far above digitization or off-site storage.
Three articles so far: a current-year budget adjustment, prior-year unpaid bills, and a police union collective bargaining agreement.

decisions.decision: Water district and Tighe & Bond presentation rescheduled to next Tuesday at 7:10 pm after Zoom disruption.
Board majority not supporting term limits; status quo kept, case-by-case reappointments, with vacancies publicized by April 1 and outreach to incumbents.
Release of 2015-2016 executive session minutes tabled two weeks; minutes available at town manager's office for review.
300th anniversary committee charge and revised appointment policy to return next week.
Zoom turned off for the rest of the meeting after intrusions; viewers directed to Facebook Live.

what_happened.line: The Select Board leaned against term limits for appointed board members and kept the current case-by-case reappointment practice.
The board appointed a full member to the Conservation Commission, passed unanimously, and ratified two town manager hires.
The water district presentation on reactivating a well was cut short by Zoom intrusions and moved to the following Tuesday.
The board approved a one-day beer and wine license and a voluntary toll fundraiser, both for Sept. 17.
The town manager reported one-time state road-repair funding that must be spent by June 30, 2023 and cannot cover police details.

why_it_matters: One-time state money for roads, sidewalks and signs has a spending deadline, so what the town picks to fix this year is decided on a fixed clock.
The appointment policy sets how vacancies on volunteer boards are advertised and filled, which affects whether a resident can seek a seat.
watch_next: The water district presentation was rescheduled to the following Tuesday at 7:10 pm.
A revised appointment policy and the 300th anniversary committee charge were due back the next week.

reconciliation.what: Our minutes against the minutes the town published. caption_error = the same fact the captions rendered badly, resolved by the official reading shown beside the as-heard one; discrepancy = a substantive difference, flagged and not resolved. Neither record is treated as the referee.
reconciliation.summary: The two records agree on the four named votes and the WRAP figures, and the board members are the same people. They differ on what else was covered: the official minutes omit the Zoom disruption, the water district presentation, term limits and the school bus and remodel figures, and our minutes omit the digitization item and the church representatives. The one thing to check first is the unnamed motion ending "manager as presented" (our Pamela as meal site manager), along with the tabling of the executive session minutes, where the two give different durations.
